# k0rdent_instances (Data Source)

Every instance in a project: the hosts its instance groups hold.

An instance is materialized when its group is created or scaled, so there is no resource for one. This is how a configuration reads a host's interfaces, whose `mac_address` or `guid` narrows a `k0rdent_file_store` grant to one interface.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The hosts one instance group holds, and a file store grant narrowed to one
# host's Ethernet interface.
data "k0rdent_instances" "trainers" {
  instance_group = k0rdent_instance_group.trainers.id
}

locals {
  # Every Ethernet MAC address in the group, keyed by instance id.
  ethernet_macs = {
    for i in data.k0rdent_instances.trainers.instances : i.id => [
      for nic in i.network_interfaces : nic.mac_address if nic.type == "ethernet"
    ]
  }
}

resource "k0rdent_file_store" "datasets" {
  id           = "datasets"
  share_type   = "general"
  capacity_gib = 1024

  consumers = {
    (k0rdent_instance_group.trainers.id) = {
      type = "instanceGroup"
      network = {
        type = "ethernet"
        # The first Ethernet MAC of the group's first host.
        mac_address = local.ethernet_macs[data.k0rdent_instances.trainers.ids[0]][0]
      }
    }
  }
}

# Only the group's running hosts.
data "k0rdent_instances" "trainers_running" {
  instance_group = k0rdent_instance_group.trainers.id
  state          = "running"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `instance_group` (String) Only return the hosts of the instance group with this id. Filtered by the platform. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `node_pool` (String) Only return the hosts provisioned into a node pool with this name. Pool names come from the ClusterType, so on its own this matches that pool in every group: set `instance_group` too for one group's pool. Filtered by the platform. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `project` (String) Project to read. Defaults to the provider's `project`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `region` (String) Region to read. Defaults to the provider's `region`. **Constraints:** Must be lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen (`[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?`), because it becomes a segment of a request URL.
- `state` (String) Return only the hosts whose `state` is this value. Sent to the platform as the list operation's own filter, and checked again on what comes back. `deleted` returns the instances the platform keeps a record of after they're gone, which an ordinary read leaves out: the platform turns its `showDeleted` on for that state. Those records are never reaped, so a long-lived group can return many. **Constraints:** Value must be one of: ["not_provisioned" "provisioning" "running" "degraded" "stopping" "stopped" "deprovisioning" "deleting" "deleted" "unknown"].

### Read-Only

- `ids` (List of String) Just the ids, for `for_each` and `contains`. Sorted by `id`, at the same positions as `instances`.
- `instances` (Attributes List) The instances, sorted by `id`. That order is stable across reads but not across a scale, so reach an element with `for_each` rather than `instances[0]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances))

<a id="nestedatt--instances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When the instance was created, as RFC 3339.
- `health` (String) Host health as the infrastructure service observes it: `healthy`, `degraded`, `unhealthy` or `unknown`. Separate from `state`: a `running` host can be `unhealthy`.
- `hostname` (String) The host's effective hostname right now. Usually `server_slug`.
- `id` (String) The instance id.
- `instance_group` (String) Id of the instance group that holds this host, the value a file store grant's `ref` takes.
- `network_interfaces` (Attributes List) The host's runtime network interfaces, as the infrastructure service reports them now. Empty until the host is provisioned. An Ethernet interface carries `mac_address` and an InfiniBand one carries `guid`, the two values a `k0rdent_file_store` grant's `consumers.network` takes to narrow it to one interface. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--instances--network_interfaces))
- `node_pool` (String) The group's node pool this host was provisioned into.
- `self_link` (String) Platform-defined reference to this instance.
- `server_slug` (String) The host's registered name.
- `state` (String) Lifecycle state, read from the host on every request: `not_provisioned`, `provisioning`, `running`, `deprovisioning`, `deleting`, `degraded` or `unknown`.
- `state_message` (String) Why the instance is in `state`. Null while `running`.
- `uid` (String) The same identity as `id`, in UUID form.

<a id="nestedatt--instances--network_interfaces"></a>
### Nested Schema for `instances.network_interfaces`

Read-Only:

- `guid` (String) GUID of an InfiniBand interface, in the `0x`-prefixed form a file store grant's `guid` takes. Null on Ethernet.
- `ip_addresses` (List of String) Addresses assigned to the interface now.
- `mac_address` (String) Hardware address of an Ethernet interface, in the colon-separated form a file store grant's `mac_address` takes. Null on InfiniBand.
- `type` (String) `ethernet` or `infiniband`.

## Related
